features.text: Katherine is 22 months old and female.
Katherine has Smith-Magenis syndrome, a chromosomal deletion.
Katherine was diagnosed with Smith-Magenis syndrome because she wasn't walking or sitting by herself at a year old.
Katherine has not walked or sat by herself by age one.
Katherine has received feeding, occupational, and physical therapy.
Katherine has excessive urination and increased fluid intake.
Katherine has approximately 8 to 10 wet diapers per day.
Katherine drinks a lot, including pea protein milk, water, and sometimes juice.
Katherine has no known discomfort or urgency during urination.
Katherine has no prior kidney function tests, such as serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, or urinalysis.
Katherine has no prior imaging studies of her kidneys or urinary tract.
There is no family history of kidney issues or genetic disorders on either the mother's or father's side.
Katherine has not had any blood tests or urinalysis, except for those done at birth.
The geneticist mentioned that some people with Smith-Magenis syndrome have problems with their legs and kidneys.
The geneticist recommended a kidney ultrasound for Katherine due to her syndrome.
The specific chromosomal deletion region associated with Katherine's Smith-Magenis syndrome is unknown to the patient.
